observed_trades.setup: One of two shorts he took despite the follow-through day; later describes Nebius as rejecting every time it gets up to the 50-day.

observed_trades.setup: Stopped out of the Nebius short right at the highs; the stock then faded and closed at lows down 13.5% today. Right idea, wrong management.
observed_trades.stop: stop was too tight; stopped at the exact high
observed_trades.quote: One of them was Nebius and I stopped out at the at the tickety-top, at the highs
observed_trades.notes: He does not say whether the stop-out was yesterday or this morning, only that 'then today' it faded; timing left blank. Repeated at 15:45 ('stop yourself out like a schmuck picture-perfect at highs').

observed_trades.setup: Second of the two shorts taken the prior day; made a couple of bucks and left it alone.
observed_trades.quote: And then AXTI effectively made a couple of bucks on this thing and then left it alone. I got short $74 yesterday.
observed_trades.notes: Covered in two pieces the next morning, see following rows.

observed_trades.setup: Woke up about seven dollars in the money on the short; covered part as it started to push back up.
observed_trades.quote: I wake up, I'm up seven bucks on it, then starts to push. I cover some, pushes some more.
observed_trades.notes: Ticker AXTI named in the preceding block (07:00). 'I wake up' = the morning after yesterday's short.

observed_trades.setup: Covered the remainder at breakeven as the stock kept pushing up.
observed_trades.quote: I take the rest off at flat and you know, kind of made that fairly easy to manage.
observed_trades.notes: Ticker AXTI named at 07:00. 'At flat' = breakeven on the short from $74; no cover price stated.

observed_trades.setup: Long HPE carried in from before; he had moved the stop to cost after yesterday's push and the morning shakeout took him out. HPE then closed near highs.
observed_trades.stop: stop moved up to cost after yesterday's push
observed_trades.quote: Let's talk about what I did today. I got knocked out of HPE on this flush out.
observed_trades.notes: Original entry date not stated in this video.

observed_trades.setup: Dell shook out into a support gap in the morning; he did not buy the low of the gap and got involved later in the day. Still in base-building mode, no breakout yet.
observed_trades.entry_basis: morning shakeout into the support gap (he entered later than the gap low)
observed_trades.quote: So, Dell uh you know, gives a nice little shakeout right into a support gap 129 bucks. You know, I wait for a little bit later to get involved
observed_trades.notes: Part of 'what I did today'. Level garbled: '129 bucks' here, '429' at 09:43; no fill price stated. Exited same day, see next row.

observed_trades.fill_timing: by the end of the day

observed_trades.notes: Ticker Dell named at 09:32. Loss of about $1.50 is a P&L figure, not a price. At 10:15 he says 'stopped out of Dell' where the context is HPE.
